preview: An internship interview experience at Citi detailing the online assessment, two technical and behavioral interview rounds, and helpful preparation tips.
content: INTERNSHIP INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE VAISHNAVI ASAWALE TY CE TIMELINE Online Presentation 1st September, 2023 6:00 pm Online Assessment 1st September, 2023 8:00 pm Arrival of List of Selected Candidates 3rd September, 2023 10:15 pm Interview Round 1 4th September, 2023 10:00 am Interview Round 2 4th September, 2023 11:30 am CRITERIA 1. CGPA of 6.5 and above 2. No active backlog PPT The PPT was conducted on 1st September, 2023 at 6:00pm. Do attend the PPT as they cover everything in detail like their values, goals, and much more. I had made a note of all the important numbers related to citi during the presentation like their number of employees, number of countries with their offices, etc, which helped me answer the “why citi?” question in the interview. They had also mentioned a rotation program over here and I made it a point to ask a question regarding this during my interview to give the impression that I had been attentive during the PPT. ONLINE ASSESSMENT The test was conducted on 1st September, 2023 at 8:00 pm on SHL. The test had 4 sections - coding, SQL, React and Angular (a few people had aptitude based questions instead of the Angular and React sections, this was probably based on the roles which had been chosen). Switching between the sections was not allowed. For the MCQ sections, you couldn’t switch between questions, nor visit a previously answered question. The test had camera and microphone proctoring. CODING SECTION: 2 coding questions were to be solved in 45 minutes. They were really easy. Everyone had different questions. Here are mine: 1. You have a freezer and multiple objects which have to be stored in this freezer. All these objects have different temperatures at which they have to be kept. These temperatures are stored in an array. You have to find the number of objects which need negative temperatures. E.g Input = [23 1 -5 33 13 -4 -11 35] Output = 3 There are 3 negative numbers in the array -5, -4 and -11. I did this using a for loop checking if the number was less than 0 and increasing a variable count. 2. You are given an array of numbers and a random number k. Sort the first k numbers of the array in ascending order and the rest in descending order. E.g. Input : Array = [22 4 1 13 21 52 3 15], k = 3 Output = [1 3 4 52 22 21 15 13] I did this using bubble sort for both, the ascending and descending part. I finished the section in around 20-25 mins. The platform was faulty as it kept giving me different number of test cases passed every time I hit ‘run’ for the same code. So, I kept on re-compiling till I could see that all test cases had been passed. Not sure if this is how it worked because they didn’t have a ‘submit code’ button. SQL: 12 questions were to be solved in 15 minutes of MCQ type. They were basic SQL queries. I had revised my DBMS Lab practicals before the test and I could manage this easily. REACT: 12 questions were to be solved in 15 minutes of MCQ type. I had no idea about React so I just went on randomly ticking answers. ANGULAR: 12 questions were to be solved in 15 minutes of MCQ type. I had no idea about Angular so I just went on randomly ticking answers. While filling up the form for citi, we were presented with 2 roles: ICG Tech and EIO&T and we had to specify our preference for these 2 roles. When the list of shortlisted candidates came on 3rd September at 10:15 pm, 20 people were shortlisted for ICG Tech; 20 people were shortlisted and 10 were waitlisted for PBWM Tech. The list for EIO&T came the next night (8 people shortlisted). INTERVIEW ROUND 1 My interview was scheduled at 10:00 am on 4th September, 2023. The interview began with the “tell me about yourself” question. He’d also told me to describe all my projects in the introduction itself. I had web-development projects on my resume where I had worked with JavaScript, Bootstrap, Node.js, Express.js and MongoDB. So, he asked me to explain some basic functionalities which could be implemented using Node.js. He asked me about some functions in MongoDB where I explained findOne(), findOneAndUpdate(), findOneAndDelete() to implement basic CRUD. He then asked how joins could be implemented in MongoDB. I told him that I had learned that if you have data which is highly relational, Mongo is of no use since joins cannot be implemented here. But he asked me the question again so I told him that I hadn’t come across any such example yet but would make it a point to look it up after the interview. He asked me if I knew the unwind operator in Mongo, I said no. He asked me if I had worked with React and Angular and I said that I hadn’t. He then asked how I had implemented the frontend of my projects. I told him HTML, CSS, JavaScript and Bootstrap. So, he wanted to know if I could design something in JavaScript if I was asked to and I told him that I was pretty confident I could. We then came to the topic of OOPS where he asked me the difference between encapsulation and data abstraction. His next question was how would I implement a chess game in C++. I said that, since in chess both the pieces, white and black had the same moves, I would define a class with these moves as the functions and would create 2 objects of this class, one pertaining to black and one for white. And if they happened to land on the ame grid, one would be eliminated based on which piece had arrived first. He asked if I knew any algorithms and where they could be implemented. I explained the sliding window algorithm, binary search, sorting algorithms (bubble sort, merge sort, selection sort and insertion sort) and Djikstra’s algorithm. I also mentioned their time complexities. He asked what I would do if I found out that something in my project was wrong just before a deadline. I explained that I was stuck in a similar situation in my first hackathon but my team and I got help from our mentors and we managed to implement the right solution after the hackathon was over. So, we learned the importance of doing more detailed research for all our subsequent work. He then asked how I would make sure that a project to be delivered to a client is good enough. I said something along the lines of always being in good contact with my team, making sure that everyone is clear with the final output to be delivered. Distribute the work and get constant updates from everyone to make sure that we are on the right track and are following set deadlines. His next question was how I would grow my connections. I replied that I would initiate conversations with people, developing bonds over common interests, even help them when required. Getting to know your seniors is also a great way to increase your network. And this can also be done via platforms like LinkedIn. He seemed pretty satisfied with the answer. He asked me if I had any questions and I asked about the tech stack I would need for my internship. It was scheduled as a 45 minute interview but it went on for 30 minutes. At around 11:05 am, a TPO CR called me to get ready for round 2. INTERVIEW ROUND 2 This round was scheduled at 11:30 am on the same day. When I joined in, my interviewer told me to wait for a few minutes as he couldn’t find my resume. The interview started with the “tell me about yourself” question. He then asked me to explain a project of mine mentioned in my resume. As I was explaining it to him, the topic of authorization came up and he asked how I was doing that. I told him that it was using Passport.js. However, this wasn’t the question he was asking. It took me around 10 minutes to understand that he was asking if I was referencing my User Schema in another schema. I was a bit disheartened that it had taken me so long to understand such a simple question but he laughed it off saying that it was fine. He also asked why I had chosen MongoDB as my database. He then asked me to take out a piece of paper and a pen and gave me a puzzle. There are 3 rooms and each room has a light bulb. There is a switchboard with all 3 switches at some distance away from these rooms. You have to find out which switch corresponds to which bulb, the constraint being that once you go to visit the rooms you can’t come back to the switchboard. I had heard of this problem before but I couldn’t recollect the solution, so I tried explaining my thought process. The ans then struck me that I could leave one bulb on for some time, then switch it off and turn on some other bulb. On visiting the rooms, I would find one bulb to be lit, one to be warm due to being on for some time and a third to be cold. He then asked me the difference between encapsulation and abstraction. What is a doubly linked list and why do we need a normal linked list if it exists. He also asked if a stack and a linked list are the same. He asked me if I was a risk taker. During the PPT, they had mentioned that they like to build upon existing solutions so I said that while I’m a combination of both, it depends mainly on the situation. With a tight deadline or an important task at hand, I would prefer to walk on the safer path but in other situations I might try taking a risk because it could lead to new and better results. He then asked if I had failed at a task in the past and had the same task at hand right now, what would I do. I said that I would consult my mentors and seniors on what the best route would be and work upon that. Then came the “why citi?” question where I mentioned some figures that had been told during the PPT. He asked me whether I had any questions and I asked him about the rotation program that had been mentioned during the PPT session as well. This round went on for 30 mins At 8:00 pm on the same day, the list of selected candidates came. 5 were selected for ICG and 5 for PBWM. On the next day, interviews for EIO&T took place and 2 were selected. TIPS 1. I used Striver’s SDE Sheet to practice coding. Do remember to revise the questions as well and make notes of the kinds of algorithms and patterns in the questions. It’s never too late to start prepping. 2. I’d watched OS and Neso Academy; and DBMS and OS from Gate Smashers while preparing for my end sems. But, I made the mistake of not making any notes so I used the above sheet for revision before the interview. Don’t leave this till the last minute as you won’t get much time to prepare when the shortlisted candidates are announced. 3. For the aptitude test preparation I’d solved the sheet given in the description of this video. 4. Frame the answers to a few basic questions like “tell me about yourself”, “what are your strengths”, “what are your weaknesses”, “where do you see yourself in a few years”, etc. Be confident while answering these. Use the STAR method to answer situation based questions. 5. Use glassdoor to read about people’s experience and interview questions. 6. Know the projects on your resume well and revise the tech stacks used in these. 7. In case you have any doubts, you can reach out to me here ALL THE BEST!! Don’t be disheartened if you aren’t selected. There are plenty of companies coming to campus. Just believe in yourself and give your best efforts.
